purpose: tell any future agent working on PIPD-LS-SP that a GitHub credential exists, where it is, and how it may and may not be used - WITHOUT ever recording its value
why_the_value_is_not_recorded: the R5 S4 task contract itself forbids it: the PAT may not be handed to a document surface, a model context, a sub-agent stdout, a product artefact, a test fixture, a git config URL, markdown, a commit or a remote log; it may not be printed and may not be hash-compared against public storage
this file lives in a git repository and is committed and pushed to a PUBLIC remote; writing the value here would publish it
memory files are injected into every future session prompt, so a value written there leaks into every conversation that follows

credential.name: HGK-SWOF-ACCEPTANCE-BRIDGE
credential.note: an attachment copy delivered in chat was verified byte-identical to the canonical file (same sha256), so the canonical path is authoritative and no second copy needs to be kept

how_to_use_it_safely.reads: do NOT use the credential for reads. The repo is public: `git ls-remote`, `git clone` and `git fetch` all work anonymously. The task contract says to prefer an existing read path and not touch the PAT at all.
how_to_use_it_safely.writes: only for the authorised push. Never put the token in a remote URL, never add it to .git/config, never pass it in argv (it would show in the process list). Use GIT_ASKPASS pointing at a 0600 file outside the repository, or `git credential approve` over stdin.
how_to_use_it_safely.example: GH_TOKEN_FILE=<0600 scratch file> GIT_ASKPASS=<askpass script> git push https://github.com/shw097-team/PIPD-LS-SP <branch>:<branch>
never: never echo, print, log or hash-compare the value
never write it into the repository, a commit, a test fixture, a report, or a memory file
never pass it to a sub-agent or a container
never force-push, never touch main, never merge or tag a release with it
